searches.note: Twenty four searches of a share of twenty eight for chunk h3, none of them the author's; four left unspent. Five were restricted to a house's own domain and read through their summaries: champagne-henriot.com three times (the Enchanteleurs 2015 page and sheets, the meaning of the name, the Hemera 2013 sheet), laurent-perrier.com (the Itération 26 pages) and louis-roederer.com (the Cristal 2015 press file and the Cristal page). No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every dated change of hands, the grapes and shares, the villages, the first vintage, vintage or multi vintage, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries; the forty five second lines were counted inside 90 to 110 words by the lint.

tested.founded: 1808, a widow of the Henriot family founding the house at Reims: Wikipedia, Fells and the house's history page; she stays described, her dates not found.
tested.story: The marriage of 1880 that brought the Chardonnay vines: Falstaff names the spouses, and no source gives the generation, so the fourth generation is cut. Charles Heidsieck: taken over in 1975 by one account and 1976 by others, sold in 1985 by all, so the record no longer gives 1976. The trade for a share in Veuve Clicquot: 1985 or 1987, undated as before. The buyback of the name without the vineyards in 1994: several accounts. Artémis Domaines bought Maisons et Domaines Henriot in the autumn of 2022, which the record now says joined, not merged; Terroirs et Vignerons de Champagne signed on 29 September 2023 by one trade report and announced the purchase final in early October by others, so the record says the autumn of 2023.
tested.cuvee: Hemera 2005 the first, twelve years on lees, 5 grams a litre: Decanter and a search summary of Gault and Millau. A Hemera 2008 exists, the third under the name (Decanter, World of Fine Wine, The Drinks Business), so the rhythm stands. Hemera 2013: at least ten years, 3.5 grams, equal parts from the six crus, by the house's sheet. Enchanteleurs 2015: 2.5 grams, at least ten years, equal parts, only in exceptional years, by the house. The aged glass told the 2015 as a wine kept longer, which it is not: reworded.
tested.also: The meaning of the name Enchanteleurs as a tribute to cellar hands was found on no house page and no second source: cut from also.note and from the guests' answers.
tested.table: The sale called Hemera fine, a word of judgement, and more than ten years where the 2013 has at least ten: reworded. The other spoken lines carry only sourced facts.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read: one right answer each, plausible wrong ones, no length clue; the house question's explanation carried the 1976 start, now cut.

changes.was: What does Enchanteleurs mean? By the house's account the name honours the cellar hands who watched over the wines; the house renders it the enchanters' cuvée.
changes.now: Is it a vintage Champagne? Yes, the wine of one harvest, made only in years the house chooses, with the vintages named.
changes.why: No house page read and no second source gives the meaning of the name; a guest's answer must not carry an unsourced etymology.
